mechanisms.behavior: The own-edition parts sheet item12 identifies the left flipper assembly. The source declares public button2/EOS4, but no retained ROM or wiring table maps the physical winding(s) to public coils. Actuators and sensors are deliberately not assigned from a commercial sibling.
mechanisms.label: Left flipper assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Own-edition item13 identifies the right flipper assembly. Public button3/EOS5 are source declarations; physical winding count, timing, contact state and coil bindings remain unresolved.
mechanisms.label: Right flipper assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Item18 establishes a three-bank in-line assembly. Reset actuator, target switch identities, sequence, home state, scoring, pulse timing and jam recovery need exact firmware and wiring evidence. No address is borrowed from a similarly themed machine.
mechanisms.label: Three-bank in-line assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Item24 names the trough kicker. The parts table item6 names a trough assembly511-1022-00; a separate bottom-components drawing prints500-1011-00 for its item6, so no single trough assembly part is promoted. Ball count, sensors, polarity and serve timing remain open.
mechanisms.label: Ball trough kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Item19 establishes a ball lock post. Its drive output, normal position, causal feedback and locking/release logic are unresolved; presence on a drawing does not bind it to a guessed coil.
mechanisms.label: Ball lock post
